body.statement:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG, let \(A_0,B_0\subseteq V\) be disjoint with \(A_0\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). Suppose \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;A_0,B_0,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) returns a proxy kernel \(H(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), with a continuous version chosen at every application of Rule L2 as required by Theorem 4.14(3). Then, pointwise on the discrete assignment domain,
\[
 H(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =P_{\mathbf M}(A_0\mid\operatorname{do}(B_0),S=\mathbf 1)
\]
for every represented \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The restriction to the positive discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\) is licensed by Remark 4.4(2).

source.locator: Theorem 4.14(3) together with Remark 4.4(2), pointwise soundness for the positive discrete specialization
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 4.14 (Main result IV: sIDP is sound). (1) Soundness up to oracle choices. If sIDP(P; A, B) does not output Fail, then for every represented model the target kernel is trackable from the selected observational kernel up to oracle choices. (3) Soundness pointwise. If sIDP(P; A, B) does not output Fail and continuous versions are chosen at each Rule L2 application, the proxy kernel equals the target pointwise.

attestation.note: Verified against Chen and Mooij, arXiv:2603.26301 PDF v1, PDF pp. 32-34, plus Remark 4.4(2) on PDF p. 27 stating M_d^+(G) is a subclass of M_c^+(G). The persisted locator names clause (1), but the node pointwise specialization requires clause (3) plus Remark 4.4(2); D-stage should repair that locator before relying on it.
